" *

* Encodes all of the provided data, starting at inPos, for inAvail bytes. Must be called at least twice: once with * the data to encode, and once with inAvail set to "-1" to alert encoder that EOF has been reached, so flush last * remaining bytes (if not multiple of 3). *

*

* Thanks to "commons" project in ws.apache.org for the bitwise operations, and general approach. * http://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/webservices/commons/trunk/modules/util/ *

* * @param in * byte[] array of binary data to base64 encode. * @param inPos * Position to start reading data from. * @param inAvail * Amount of bytes available from input for encoding. "

The failing test `testEncoder` in the `org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64Codec13Test` class is testing the `encode` method of the `Base64` class from Apache Commons Codec.

The current bug report states that the instance `encode()` method of `Base64` appends a CRLF and chunks the output into 76-character lines. This behavior is different from Commons-Codec-1.3, which did not exhibit this behavior. The static `Base64.encodeBase64()` method behaves the same in both versions, so the issue only affects the instance `encode()` method.

By looking at the source code of the `org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64.encode(byte[], int, int)` method, we can see that the method encodes the provided data in chunks of 3 bytes and adds padding if necessary. It also contains logic to handle EOF and flush remaining bytes if the input is not a multiple of 3 bytes. Additionally, the method includes logic to add line separators after every 76 characters if the `lineLength` is specified.

The observed behavior of appending a CRLF and chunking the output into 76-character lines is likely related to the logic implemented in the `encode` method. It seems that the method is designed to add line separators to the encoded output to conform to the specified line length requirement, which results in the observed behavior.

To address the reported issue of the instance `encode()` method appending a CRLF and chunking the output into 76-character lines, the logic in the `encode` method may need to be adjusted to align with the behavior of Commons-Codec-1.3, which did not exhibit this behavior. This could involve modifying the encoding logic to remove the automatic line length enforcement or provide an option to disable it.

In conclusion, the root cause of the bug is the encoding logic in the `encode` method of the `Base64` class, which appends a CRLF and chunks the output into 76-character lines. Adjustments may be needed to restore the behavior to match that of Commons-Codec-1.3.

Next, I will suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed.
```java
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64.encode(byte[], int, int)
```
